description: Journey — while composing, and to fix what gripforge_game_audit reports (its defects carry the exact config to write). Tune an installed kit: merge config values validated against the kit configSchema (read it with gripforge_gamekit_get), or patch the config as a document (patch: set a nested key, add / change / remove one element of a list without rewriting it), or toggle enabled to switch the kit off without uninstalling it. Configure installed kits freely rather than recoding what they do (game.engine: startScene, startEntry, flow.title, story flags). The interface look of a game is ui.theme: set preset (scifi-lowpoly, military, fantasy-medieval, cyberpunk-neon, cartoon-bright, horror-dark, minimal-clean, retro-pixel) for a complete look, and only the colours, typography, shapes or glyphs that must differ (they win over the preset); gripforge_game_theme_from_concept fills it from the art direction. Switching game.engine off follows the confirmation of a removal: the first call answers 409 confirm_required with details.confirm; send it back with enabled=false after the user agreed — never on your own. Returns { kit, project } with the new project revision. Call this AFTER gripforge_gamekit_install. 0 credits.

config.description: Kit config values, validated against the kit configSchema returned by gripforge_gamekit_get. Merged over the current config.

confirm.description: game.engine enabled=false: the confirm token of the previous answer.

enabled.description: false to disable the kit at runtime while keeping it installed; true to re-enable.

id.description: Kit id from the catalogue, dotted (e.g. vehicle.driveable, mission.objectives).

patch.description: The config as a document, instead of rewriting a whole list: { set: { "<dotted path>": value }, append: { "<path of a list>": [items] }, update: { "<path>": [{ match: { key: value }, set: { … } }] }, remove: { "<path>": [values or { key: value }] } } — add, change or remove one element of a config list (an item with the id of an element replaces it); a list the project does not write starts from the kit default. Validated against the configSchema like config.

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

reason.description: One sentence: why you do this, recorded in the project history (required in spirit when you go against the installed-kits rule).

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.

name: gripforge_gamekit_configure
title: Configure an installed Game Kit
